public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim says concern about AI's threat to the information ecosystem had gone mainstream by April 2024. In January 2024 the World Economic Forum ranked misinformation the top short-term global risk and said AI-driven misinformation dominated its 2024 outlook. An October 2023 AP-NORC poll found 58% of US adults expected AI to increase election misinformation. Both show broad awareness shortly before the post. One caveat: the same poll found 54% of adults had not heard much about AI at all. Also, no cited source measures the change directly.
limitations: The trend ('more broadly') is inferred from high levels, not from a measured before-and-after comparison.
The claim is soft and has no named measure; a stricter reading that demands a measured rise could leave it unresolved.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Awareness of the danger generative AI poses to the information ecosystem is finally spreading more widely.

statement.excerpt: The good news is that word is finally getting out more broadly.

our_interpretation: Read as: by early April 2024, concern about generative AI's threat to the information ecosystem had moved beyond specialists into mainstream institutions and the general public.
Signs that count: major mainstream risk rankings and national polls from the months before the post that treat AI-driven misinformation as a leading concern.
Period chosen: October 2023 to the post date, the latest months public evidence could report on before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Mainstream bodies or representative polls from late 2023 to early April 2024 show AI-driven misinformation widely recognised as a major concern.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Polls or rankings from that period show little public or institutional awareness of AI misinformation risk, or awareness falling.

evidence.excerpt: Concerns over a persistent cost-of-living crisis and the intertwined risks of AI-driven misinformation and disinformation, and societal polarization dominated the risks outlook for 2024.
evidence.locator: section 'Rise of disinformation and conflict', paragraph 1
evidence.explanation: A major mainstream body said AI-driven misinformation dominated its 2024 risk outlook, three months before the post. That shows the concern had reached the mainstream.

evidence.excerpt: Misinformation and disinformation are biggest short-term risks
evidence.locator: summary line at top of release
evidence.explanation: More than 1,400 surveyed experts ranked misinformation first among short-term global risks, a sign of very broad institutional concern.

evidence.excerpt: Most adults (58%) believe that the use of AI will increase the spread of misinformation during the 2024 presidential election
evidence.explanation: A representative US poll found most adults expected AI to increase election misinformation. Concern was widespread among the public, not just experts.

evidence.excerpt: Overall, 54% of adults have not read or heard much at all about AI
evidence.explanation: A caveat: many adults still knew little about AI itself, so public awareness was uneven.
